problem:
$$
{∬}_{D}\boxed{}\,\text{d}A,\,D={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le \pi }
$$

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $r(u,v)=⟨2u\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,3u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u⟩$ for $0\le u\le 1$ and $0\le v\le \pi .$ What is the missing expression?

examples.knowledge_point: Finding an Integral That Represents the Surface Area of a Parametric Surface
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14065243/assets/95e3f2da04e23c9b42ea04cba3ee1d7cc069fef992592f09a70cef367b670f0d.png)

The integral above gives the surface area of the parametric surface $\mathbf{r}(u,v) = \big\langle u, \: v, \: u^3-v \big\rangle$ for $0 \leq u \leq 3$ and $0 \leq v \leq 2.$ What is the missing expression?
examples.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $\mathbf r (u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
\iint\limits_S \,\textrm d S = \iint\limits_D  \left\|  \mathbf{r}'_u \times \mathbf{r}'_v \right\|  \text{d}A.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{3}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,3{u}^{2}⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{3}-v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3{u}^{2} \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-3{u}^{2},\,1,\,1⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

and its magnitude is

$$
\begin{aligned}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖ & =‖⟨-3{u}^{2},\,1,\,1⟩‖ \\  & =\sqrt{(3{u}^{2})^{2}+(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{u}^{4}+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface area is

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}‖{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}‖\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{9{u}^{4}+2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the fundamental vector product of the surface defined by the equations 

$$
x={u}^{2}+1,\,y={v}^{3}+1,\,z=2u+v.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
For a surface with parametrization $r(u,v),$ the fundamental vector product is defined as ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}.$

In vector form, our surface has the equation 

$$
r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2}+1,\,{v}^{3}+1,\,2u+v⟩.
$$

We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}({v}^{3}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(2u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,0,\,2⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}({v}^{3}+1),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(2u+v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,3{v}^{2},\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2u & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 3{v}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 3{v}^{2} & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2u & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2u & 0 \\ 0 & 3{v}^{2}\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨-6{v}^{2},\,-2u,\,6u{v}^{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
